Are you passionate about improving outcomes for people leaving prison and making sure they receive the right support when they return to the community?

- Ensuring alert forms and key information are shared with community services so that support can continue without unnecessary delays.
- Building strong relationships with local authority and community substance misuse teams, developing effective referral pathways and joint-working arrangements.
- Keeping up to date with local community treatment offers and ensuring prison teams have the information they need to support successful referrals.
- Establishing and chairing continuity of care forums, bringing partners together to identify challenges, share learning and improve outcomes.
- Producing accurate meeting minutes, actions and progress updates, ensuring agreed improvements are followed through.
- Acting as a key point of contact for community prison in-reach workers, helping them overcome barriers and supporting effective pre-release reviews.
- Leading regional NDTMS and other relevant audits, identifying opportunities to improve data quality and performance.
- Supporting the organisation of release fairs and events within the prison, helping service users connect with community support.
- Regularly reviewing and updating the Continuity of Care Best Practice Framework, ensuring it reflects current guidance and good practice.
- Developing strong community partnerships that improve continuity of care and outcomes for service users.
- Working collaboratively with Health and Justice colleagues, NHSE and OHID to support the delivery of commissioning projects and initiatives.
- Sharing best practice, progress and learning with managers and teams across the region.

What we are looking for

We're looking for someone who is passionate about partnership working and committed to making a real difference to people moving from prison back into the community.

You'll ideally bring:
- Experience of working within substance misuse, health, criminal justice or a related setting.
- A strong understanding of the challenges people can face when transitioning from prison into community services.
- Excellent communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to work confidently with a wide range of partners.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage audits, meetings, actions and deadlines effectively.
- Excellent attention to detail, particularly when working with data, records and performance information.
- The confidence to chair meetings, influence others and drive actions forward.
- Experience of working collaboratively across different organisations and professional teams.
- The ability to identify barriers, find practical solutions and continuously look for ways to improve services.
- A proactive and motivated approach, with the confidence to work independently while also being a strong team player.
- A commitment to person-centred support, equality and improving outcomes for people affected by substance misuse and the criminal justice system.
- The flexibility to travel between London sites when required.

This is more than an administrative coordination role. You'll have the opportunity to shape how continuity of care is delivered across London, strengthen relationships between prison and community services, and help ensure people leaving custody have the support they need to move forward.

If you're passionate about partnership working, improving services and making a meaningful difference to people's lives, we'd love to hear from you. Travel across London may be required.

The Company

I'm working with a successful international consumer goods business that's continuing to grow across global markets.

They're looking for another person to join a close-knit team at the heart of their international operations, connecting customers, overseas manufacturing partners and internal teams.

I've recruited for the business for a number of years and it's one where people genuinely enjoy working. The culture is collaborative, there's a real buzz around the office and people tend to build long-term careers because they enjoy the variety, the people and the opportunities to grow.

The Opportunity

This is a particularly exciting time to join the team. Positive changes within the business have created what is essentially a new role, giving the person joining a genuine opportunity to help shape how the department works as it develops.

You'll get great exposure across the business, working with international customers, colleagues in the US, manufacturing partners in Asia and teams across Sales, Planning and Supply Chain. You'll be close to the full process, seeing how customer requirements translate through purchasing and production and ultimately through to delivery.

But the real opportunity is to make the role your own. The team is looking for someone who will spot where things could work better, bring ideas and solutions and help shape new ways of working rather than simply following processes that have always been there.

You'll have plenty of autonomy and the chance to use your judgement. Priorities can change quickly and problems won't always have an obvious answer, so this will suit someone who's naturally curious, asks the right questions and enjoys working out the best way forward.

For someone who wants to broaden their experience, get closer to different areas of an international business and have a genuine voice in how a growing function develops, there's a lot of opportunity here.

The Role

Day to day you'll be:
- Coordinating international customer requirements through purchasing, production and delivery.
- Supporting forecasting and planning to keep customer requirements, purchasing and production aligned.
- Working with international teams and overseas manufacturing partners to coordinate purchasing and production.
- Making sure orders are accurate, with the right quantities, information and required dates.
- Tracking production and supply, identifying potential delays or issues and finding solutions.
- Working closely with Sales, Planning, Supply Chain and Procurement.
- Building strong customer relationships and providing clear, accurate updates.
- Managing different customer and market requirements.
- Finding practical solutions when timings, quantities or production requirements create challenges.
- Keeping product, customer and supply information accurate.
- Looking for ways to improve processes and make things work better.

The Person

There are several backgrounds that could work well here. You may come from international customer or commercial operations, or your experience might sit closer to buying, merchandising, planning, production or supply chain.

What's important is that you've had exposure to both the customer side and some of what happens further upstream to make those orders possible.

That could include:
- Working with international customers, wholesale accounts or distributors.
- Working with overseas suppliers, factories or manufacturing partners.
- Purchasing, production or supply coordination.
- Critical paths, lead times, stock and availability.
- Planning, forecasting or working closely with planning teams.
- Coordinating across Sales, Supply Chain, Operations or other internal teams.
- Identifying problems, working through the options and finding practical solutions.

You don't need every one of these, but you should understand that getting a customer order right involves more than processing it and arranging delivery.

This also isn't a pure supply chain or production role. You'll work closely with international customers and commercial teams, so you'll need to be a confident communicator who enjoys building relationships as much as getting into the detail.

You'll need to come from a product-led environment such as consumer goods, FMCG, retail, fashion, beauty, homeware or something similar.

Above all, we're looking for someone who thinks ahead, joins the dots and takes ownership. Someone with good judgement, strong attention to detail and the confidence to spot when something doesn't quite add up and work out what to do about it.

If you're looking for a busy, varied role where you'll be trusted, challenged and given the opportunity to put your stamp on something, I'd love to hear from you.

description: We are currently looking for a hardworking and enthusiastic individual to join our friendly, GP Practice team in East London as a Receptionist. The post-holder will be responsible for dealing with telephone calls and checking patients in with their appointments, helping patients with their queries and undertaking admin tasks in the Practice. The role is suitable for someone who has admin and primary care work experience and they must be able to multi-task, hold excellent communication skills and has a passion for helping patients and able to provide excellent customer service. The main role of the receptionist is to receive, assist and direct patients and visitors in the Practice in a professional, courteous, and effective way. The individual must be able to provide general assistance to the Practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and visitors, both in person and via telephone. The individual must also be able to support the Practice team by supporting and undertaking in administrative duties. Reception duties: 1) Ensure an effective and efficient reception service is provided to patients and any other visitors to the Practice. 2) Deal with all general enquiries, explain procedures and make new and follow-up appointments. 3) Using your own judgment and communication skills ensure that patients with no prior appointment but who need urgent consultation are seen in a logical and non-disruptive manner. 4) Explain Practice arrangements and formal requirements to new patients and those seeking temporary cover and ensure procedures are completed. 5) Receive and make telephone calls as required. Divert calls and take messages, ensuring accuracy of detail and prompt appropriate delivery. 6) Action repeat prescription requests and ensure that they are ready for collection by the patient within 48 hours, in line with Practice protocol. 7) Take action on clinicians requests for further information/patient contact information etc. (including computerised practice notes), ensuring completion of all associated paperwork. 8) Advise patients of relevant charges for private (non-General Medical Services) services, accept payment and issue receipts for same. 9) Enter patient information on to the computer as required. 10) Prepare clinical rooms for surgeries, supply prescription forms and record numbers in use and ensure adequate supplies of consumables (including bottles, couch rolls, test request forms etc.).
